data_card.measured: Surveyed high-water marks (USGS documented 267, of which 254 were surveyed) and mapped inundation polygons and depth rasters for seven North Carolina communities, October 2016.
data_card.method: USGS post-flood field survey of high-water marks; inundation and depth surfaces interpolated from the marks and terrain.
data_card.uncertainty: Each mark carries a USGS quality rating; to be recorded per mark when the reference is built.
known_issues: The mapped extent is derived from the same marks, so it is not independent evidence.
Use constraints to be confirmed in the release metadata (US government data are usually public domain).
data_card.exercises: Riverine floodplain inundation over real terrain: conveyance, storage and peak levels.
data_card.cannot_tell: Peak marks do not show timing, and the inflow hydrograph and roughness are themselves uncertain, so a miss can come from the boundary data as much as the model.

events.notes: Single event; teams may calibrate only against upstream gauged stages, never the marks.

validation_design.holdout_policy: The marks are public, so the holdout is by rule: calibration may use gauge records only, and each submission declares that in its configuration.
